Politics is once again front and center.

Just a short while back, a very combative Mamata Banerjee, the Bengal Chief Minister, called on Union Home Minister Rajnath Singh, and she warned him of bloodshed and mayhem if the NRC exercise were to be carried out in her state, the state of Bengal.
This, after the BJP hinted that after Assam, Bengal would be the next state where there will be a national register of citizens,
that will be put out.
First up on Face Off, let's take you through the five big developments that have happened on this very very important story.
It had resonance both in the corridors of parliament as well as right across the length and breadth of this country.
Number one, Mamata Banerjee and she has become the face of the opposition on this story.
She today was in Delhi a day after the NRC list was made public.
She met with Union Home Minister Rajnath Singh on this NRC question.
She reportedly told him
that there would be a civil war if this exercise were extended to Bengal.

The Home Minister in reply simply said that no individual, no one will be disturbed, no one will be inconvenienced with this NRC exercise and that there are multiple options still left, multiple avenues still left even for the 40 lakh people who are in that list.
We also got the first reaction from Bangladesh.
This is the first official reaction from Sheikh Hasina's government.
The information minister Islam ul Haq Eno has spoken exclusively to CNN News 18, and he says, look, this is your problem.
This is not ours.
This is India's internal problem.
These 40 lakh citizens are not Bangladeshi citizens.
They are your citizens, and it's for you to figure it out.
Number three, and this is where the entire NRC exercise itself has lost its credibility because someone as

Let's say, I wouldn't say high profile, but certainly someone who is known, former President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed, who hails from Assam, his family, his kin are alleging that they are not there in the NRC list.
If somebody who's got this kind of lineage, someone who went on to become the president of India, occupy the highest constitutional office in this country, if his family relatives are saying,
we're not there in the NRC list, then what credibility does this exercise have, does this list have?

But, like I said, it's politics front and center, Amit Shah, both in Parliament and outside today, taking the attack to the opposition, simply asking one question, and thereby there is an equivalence also that he's drawn.
He's simply asking the opposition, by opposing the NRC, by obstructing Parliament, are you sending out a message that you want to save
illegal Bangladeshi immigrants?
That's the question the BJP National President is asking.

And the reason why that question is coming to the fore now, not just in Assam, it's spreading to other states as well, most notably in Bengal, is because BJP's General Secretary in charge of Bengal, Kailash Vijayvarghya, he says Bengal is going to be the next stop.
in the NRC list.
